messages.content: Use web search to find relevant datasets. Only include landing pages or DOIs. Do not invent links. Do not call time, date, timestamp, or clock tools.

Query: Can you find datasets about Crime and law enforcement in Germany during the 1970s, matching this research need: Survey data on public attitudes toward the death penalty for murder, with demographic variables such as age, sex, marital status, religion, education, occupation, income, household composition, city size, and state.
Respond ONLY as JSON in this exact shape: {"items":[{"title":"...","url_or_doi":"...","justification":"..."}]}. Put any DOI, URL, landing page, or link in url_or_doi.

queries: site:search.gesis.org death penalty murder 1970 Germany survey marital status city size
ZA survey Germany 1970s death penalty murder demographic religion income state survey dataset
action.query: site:search.gesis.org death penalty murder 1970 Germany survey marital status city size

content.text: {"items":[{"title":"Politbarometer 1988 (Cumulative Dataset), ZA1762","url_or_doi":"https://access.gesis.org/dbk/1635","justification":"German public opinion survey containing questions about support for introducing the death penalty, including for murder and politically motivated murder. Relevant to research on capital punishment attitudes and demographic differences. However, the survey was conducted in 1988 rather than the 1970s, making it a supplementary historical comparison rather than an exact match."},{"title":"German General Social Survey (ALLBUS) – Cumulation 1980–2014, ZA4584","url_or_doi":"https://search.gesis.org/research_data/ZA4584?lang=de","justification":"Large-scale German social survey dataset covering political attitudes, criminal justice opinions, and demographic characteristics. Includes questions concerning capital punishment for terrorists and harsher criminal penalties. Contains demographic variables useful for studying differences across social groups. Coverage begins in 1980, so it does not directly satisfy the requested 1970s period, and its death-penalty questions are not necessarily specific to murder."}]}
